messages:
jamie: Heads up — after landing the packing+swap change on the co-residency branch, we've seen a regression for small-chat latency p95 on 3090 nodes. It only shows up when 2 models share the card (7B + 2B).

ravi: can you paste the profiler output? curious if it's allocator churn or kernel dispatch overhead.

jamie: here's the perf snapshot from the nightly run (trimmed):
```
allocator: pool_allocs=482k pool_frees=470k fragmentation=14.8% HWM=12.6GB reserved=16.0GB
kv_cache: hits=89.4% miss=10.6% avg_kv_alloc=128KB reuse_rate=62%
batching: avg_batch=4.2 target=8 effective_latency_ms=42.1
kernel_select: chosen_kernel=matmul_fused_mk8 fallback=cuda_gemm_sm70 latency_diff=+3.4ms
context_switches: swap_in=121 swap_out=109 swap_latency_avg_ms=6.8
```

ravi: interesting — fragmentation not huge, but swap_count ~120 looks suspicious. If KV cache reuse is 62% we're wasting copies on swap. Could be workspace sizing per-model causing repeated allocations when switching.

anya: ping — this sounds like batcher heuristics interacting with co-residency. When avg_batch is 4 and target 8, we may be forcing microbatches and triggering frequent context prewarm/swap. Do we have per-model min_workspace pinned?

jamie: currently min_workspace is dynamic based on peak sequence length per-model. We disabled static reservation to increase packing efficiency. That probably freed VRAM but caused fragmentation and repeated re-reserves on swap.

mike: quick idea: introduce a light-weight per-model soft_reserve (e.g., 256MB) for KV+workspace to reduce churn. It keeps base footprint per slot without blocking packing.

laura: +1 for soft_reserve. Also worth trying a cache-first swap: prefer evicting inactive KV pages before whole-model swap. That would keep kernel code resident.

ravi: agree. Also kernel selection: the profiler line kernel_select delta +3.4ms suggests we fall back to a slower kernel when certain workspace sizes are available. We should add kernel profiles to our model metadata so routing can pick variants with kernels that match available workspace.

jamie: I ran an A/B where I set soft_reserve=256MB for the 7B model and changed batching target to 6. Results: p95 dropped from 185ms -> 142ms, swap_count down to 38, KV reuse up to 78%.

anya: that's encouraging. Can you paste the exact env flags? We need to reproduce in CI.

jamie: flags used: `--soft-reserve-mb=256 --batch-target=6 --kv-evict-threshold=0.6 --alloc-compact=true`

ravi: `alloc-compact=true` is doing a lot here — forces free-list compaction after swap which reduces fragmentation but costs CPU. What's the CPU impact?

jamie: CPU frontend time increased ~4% but overall throughput improved. For our SLOs that's acceptable.

laura: long-term we should avoid global compacting. Proposal: compact only the free list buckets above a size threshold when fragmentation >12% OR when swap_count > 50 in last minute. That gives targeted compaction.

mike: also worth tracking per-model swap hotness metric and pin hot models to a small resident heap. Hotness = KV hits / last_60s_reqs. If >0.75, prevent swap unless OOM imminent.

anya: actionable checklist: 1) prod A/B with soft_reserve 256MB for multi-model hosts (jamie) 2) add kernel profile metadata and plumb routing heuristics (ravi) 3) implement targeted compaction (laura) 4) implement KV-first-eviction strategy + hotness metric (mike).

jamie: I'll run A/B tomorrow on canary pool and upload flamegraphs.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-4123: "co-residency: soft_reserve experiment + KV-first eviction" assigned to jamie, ravi, laura, mike. <https://tracker/redwood/INF-4123> :white_check_mark:

ravi: one more note — when adding kernel metadata, include expected workspace ranges. Example entry: `kernels: [{name: matmul_fused_mk8, workspace_range_mb: [64,512], perf_ns: 2100}, ...]` so the router can choose compatible kernels during packing.

laura: I'll draft the targeted compaction PR. Will add a flag `--compact-threshold-pct=12` and `--compact-bucket-min=8MB`.

mike: for KV-first eviction, ensure we can stream evicted KV to host memory rather than immediate disk swap — that was killing latency in previous tests. Prefer host pinned memory transfer async.

jamie: noted. Thanks team, will post CI links and flamegraphs in this thread when available. :rocket:

mike: :thumbsup: keep an eye on the 2B tail latency too — smaller models are sensitive to kernel choice even when they seem cheap.

laura: agreed. We'll also add a small microbenchmark that cycles two models co-resident and measures swap latency under different soft_reserve sizes.

jamie: final note — regression only hits when packing density >1.2x (more than one model per card). Single-model hosts unchanged. So this is definitely co-residency interaction.

ravi: perfect. priority = high for infra perf. Let's sync tomorrow 9:30am PT.

jamie: thanks all, logging off for tonight.
